title: The Ocean Looketh Up to Heaven
description: The Ocean Looketh Up to Heaven in Tonic Solfa to ST ANNE, doh is C: the solfa with the words, staff notation, 5 verses and a piano.
about: John Greenleaf Whittier wrote these words. They were printed in A Book of Hymns for Public and Private Devotion, compiled by Samuel Longfellow and Samuel Johnson (Boston, 1848), as hymn 85, “Nature's Worship”.
The book printed the words without tunes, marked Common Metre (8.6.8.6), to be sung to any tune of that metre. This page sets them to ST ANNE; any other Common Metre tune fits them as well.
underlay: Th'o-cean loo-keth up to hea-ven, As 'twere a liv-ing thing; The hom-age of its waves is given, In cease-less wor-ship-ping.

lines: The ocean looketh up to heaven,
The homage of its waves is given,
They kneel upon the sloping sand
The mists are lifted from the rills,
Like the white wing of prayer;
They kneel above the ancient hills,
As if a prayerful spirit passed
The sky is as a temple's arch:
Is glorious with the spirit march

source: A Book of Hymns for Public and Private Devotion (1848)
licence: Public domain: John Greenleaf Whittier died in 1892.
credits: Words by John Greenleaf Whittier (1807–1892), public domain, as printed in A Book of Hymns for Public and Private Devotion (1848); set to ST ANNE by NoteFusion, as words-only hymn books were sung.
